title: Getting married
summary: This page provides information on the processes for getting married, registering relationships, and changing names in NSW.
who_can_apply: Must apply for a Notice of Intended Marriage before getting married.
Must apply to get married at a Registry Office.

more_info.text: Notice of Intended Marriage applicationBefore you get married you, must complete a Notice of Intended Marriage and give it to your authorised celebrant. This needs to be done at least a month prior to the wedding date.

Apply to get married at a Registry OfficeThe Registry conducts wedding ceremonies at a number of locations around Sydney, and will take care of all the legal requirements for you, from ceremony to certificate.
Apply for a single status certificateA single status certificate verifies that you've not been married in NSW during a specified period of time.
Request a proof of divorce orderYou can request a search of the records of the Family Court of Australia and the Federal Circuit Court of Australia to prove that a divorce was granted and finalised.

faqs.q: How do I start the process of getting married?
faqs.a: You must first apply for a Notice of Intended Marriage. You can apply online using the Notice of Intended Marriage application link.
You can apply to get married at a Registry Office.

faqs.q: What if I am divorced and need to prove it?
faqs.a: You can request a proof of divorce order.

faqs.q: How do I register a relationship in NSW?
faqs.a: You can apply to register a relationship in NSW. If you need to withdraw this application, you can use the withdrawal link.
